paper: Blackwell et al. 2021, PLoS Biology 19(11): e3001421 (661k bacterial genomes snapshot)
note: Open questions genuinely not answered by this replication. Each is grounded in a specific claim or method choice in the paper or in the delivered artifacts, not general critique.

open_questions.q: Does re-running the archived Unicycler-primary/SPAdes-fallback wrapper (github.com/iqbal-lab-org/assemble-all-ena) on the same ENA accession list independently regenerate the delivered contigs.fa.gz files within a defined similarity tolerance?
open_questions.basis: Claim C7 in REPORT.md is explicitly excluded from this replication (~30k CPU-months). The 25-sample MD5 audit verifies delivery of the FASTA files but not derivation from raw reads. A pipeline-level replication of even 100 samples end-to-end (SRA reads -> Unicycler -> QUAST/CheckM -> compare to delivered assembly + high_quality flag) would close this.
next_steps: Pull the 100-sample subset used in this spot-check plus 75 more (n=100) FASTQ reads from ENA/SRA
Re-run the assemble-all-ena wrapper at pinned commit on those reads
Compute assembly similarity to delivered files (N50, total-bp, contig count, ANI via skani or mash) and compare to paper's own reported per-sample QC in File4
Report per-sample delta distribution and identify any systematic drift (e.g. new SPAdes/Unicycler versions)

open_questions.q: How much of the 2,336 vs 2,594 species-count delta between the paper's HQ set and this replication's full 661k set is explained by Kraken2/Bracken calls on low-quality assemblies, versus other causes such as taxonomy database drift between the paper's snapshot and the current NCBI taxonomy?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md 4.2 attributes the Delta=258 species to 21,424 dropped low-quality assemblies contributing spurious rare-species Kraken calls, but does not actually recount species restricted to high_quality==TRUE. If Kraken's reference DB or NCBI taxonomy has been updated since 2021, some of the delta could be relabelling rather than QC-driven noise.
next_steps: Inner-join File2_taxid_lineage_661K.txt to File4_QC_characterisation_661K.txt on sample_id
Recount unique species restricted to high_quality==TRUE; check whether it exactly equals 2,336

If the count does not exactly reproduce, diff the species list against NCBI taxonomy dumps from 2018-11 vs current to quantify how many entries are taxonomy-drift artefacts (renamed / merged / split taxa)
Report the decomposition: QC-attributable vs taxonomy-drift-attributable

open_questions.q: Do the Kraken2/Bracken species labels in File2 agree with an independent modern classifier (e.g. GTDB-Tk r220) on a genome-quality-controlled subsample, particularly for the ~10% of assemblies not in the top-20 pathogens where classification confidence is likely lower?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md Genuine Critique #2 flags that both File2 labels and ENA SCIENTIFIC_NAME trace back to the same submitter/Kraken lineage; no truly independent classifier was applied. Claim C3 (2,336 species) rides entirely on Kraken calls being correct.
next_steps: Draw a stratified subsample of ~500 high_quality genomes weighted toward the tail (below rank 20) of File2
Run GTDB-Tk classify_wf against release r220 on that subsample
Compare species-level calls; compute confusion matrix vs File2 Kraken labels
Report agreement rate overall and per-genus, and enumerate any tail species that GTDB-Tk collapses or splits differently

open_questions.q: Does the published COBS index (872 GB) correctly return the expected sample_id hits for a set of known query k-mers derived from AMR genes, MLST alleles, and plasmid replicons that are catalogued in the paper's own per-genome AMRFinder/plasmid metadata?
open_questions.basis: Claim C5 verified that the COBS artefact is downloadable, but no functional round-trip test was run: given a k-mer that the paper's own annotation says should be present in a specified set of samples, does querying the COBS index return that set? This is the paper's headline user-facing capability (searchable snapshot) and it is currently untested end-to-end.
next_steps: From File4/AMR-metadata pick 20 AMR genes (e.g. blaCTX-M-15, mecA, van variants) with well-defined presence sets across the 661k samples
Extract representative k-mers (k=31) for each
Query the COBS index via the paper's documented client for each k-mer set; capture returned sample_id list
Compare returned lists to the ground-truth presence lists from the metadata; report recall, precision, and any systematic false-negative pattern (e.g. species-restricted misses)

open_questions.q: Are the paper's Rnotebooks (which reproduce every figure) still runnable against the current Figshare files and the current CRAN/Bioconductor stack, and if so do the regenerated Fig 1B/C match the panels in the published PDF pixel-adjacently?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md 1 lists Rnotebooks as artefact (v) of the paper; the replication did not execute them (Genuine Critique #8). Re-running them would independently confirm C4 and the plasmid/AMR figures without going through raw metadata files, and would surface any package-drift breakage that future users would hit.
next_steps: Locate the Rnotebook repo referenced in the paper's Data Availability / Code Availability statement
Rebuild the notebook environment (renv.lock if present; else best-effort with R 4.x + noted Bioconductor version)
Execute all notebooks against the same Figshare 16437939 files used here
Diff the regenerated Fig 1B/C against the published PDF; log any package errors or numerical drift
